claims.text: The initial FeCoNi alloy is single-phase FCC.
Coarse-grained single-phase FCC FeCoNi has coercivity below 100 Oe.
Room-temperature HPT at approximately 6 GPa for 5–10 rotations, followed by low-temperature annealing, will produce a nanocrystalline FeCoNi structure.
The proposed HPT treatment will create a high density of dislocations.
The proposed treatment will create ultrafine grain boundaries.
The HPT-induced defects and ultrafine grain boundaries will act as domain-wall pinning centers.
Defect-mediated impediment of domain-wall motion will increase coercivity.
Annealing at 300–400 °C for approximately 30 minutes will relieve excessive strain.
The low-temperature anneal will partially recover magnetic order.
The low-temperature anneal will retain enough of the HPT-induced defect structure to preserve enhanced domain-wall pinning.
The combined HPT and annealing treatment will raise coercivity substantially above 100 Oe relative to coarse-grained FeCoNi.
The combined treatment will preserve saturation magnetization to within 10% of the coarse-grained baseline.
Annealing below 400 °C is necessary to prevent undesirable grain growth.
Annealing below 400 °C is necessary to prevent phase transformation.
An inert atmosphere will avoid oxidation and maintain alloy composition during annealing.
The intervention is applicable to closely related FCC FeCoNi-derived high-entropy alloys as well as FeCoNi itself.

contradictions.description: The boundary states that annealing must remain below 400 °C, whereas the stated processing range includes 400 °C and the experiment explicitly tests samples at 400 °C.
